note: lxpt floor core v1 (spec/floor-v1.md). Generated by python/gen_core_fixtures.py from the Python reference; every value is a TEST value. Each scenario builds one Floor (role, channel_tag, capacity, talk_limit_s) over Counters of 'talkers' entries, then runs its steps in order: 'do' names the event, 'at' is the clock in ms, the other fields are its inputs (byte fields as hex). 'expect' is every line the step produced: the floor actions in order, then 'forward'/'drop' for a frame and 'new'/'seen' for a release, then 'holder <who>/<spurt>' or 'holder -'.

scenarios.name: settle_then_grant
scenarios.note: a local claim is held for the settle window, then granted

scenarios.name: busy_and_retries
scenarios.note: a claim on a held floor gets BUSY, a retry BUSY again, the holder's retry a GRANT

scenarios.name: settle_orders_by_hash
scenarios.note: two local claims inside the window: the order decides, not arrival

scenarios.name: remote_pending_blocks
scenarios.note: a remote claim that orders first holds a local one until its TALKING

scenarios.name: remote_hold_expires
scenarios.note: with no evidence, a remote claim stops blocking after 600 ms

scenarios.name: remote_after_order_does_not_block
scenarios.note: a remote claim that orders later does not hold a local one

scenarios.name: remote_live_by_frame
scenarios.note: a known remote claim goes live on its first FRAME

scenarios.name: merge_yield_soft
scenarios.note: two live spurts: the one that orders later yields, and comes back if the winner leaves while it is still talking

scenarios.name: preempt_verified
scenarios.note: a verified commander's claim cuts a member at the end of its window

scenarios.name: rights_table
scenarios.note: leader cuts member, deputy cuts leader, commander cuts deputy; equal tiers never cut, nobody cuts upward

scenarios.name: unverified_tiers
scenarios.note: an unverified commander orders as a member and cuts nobody

scenarios.name: emergency
scenarios.note: unverified Emergency takes only an idle floor; two Emergency spurts never cut; a verified Emergency cuts any spurt without it

scenarios.name: quiet_lost_resume
scenarios.note: silence: quiet at 1.2 s, lost at 5 s; continuing frames within the resume window resume; old ones do not

scenarios.name: lost_expires
scenarios.note: a lost spurt not resumed within the 2 s resume window ends; its later frames are dropped

scenarios.name: resume_window_edges
scenarios.note: a frame received 1999 ms after the loss resumes; one received 2000 ms after it is dropped, and the spurt ends at that tick

scenarios.name: resume_window_counts_rx
scenarios.note: the window is judged on when a frame was received: one queued during the relay's own stall, received inside the window, still resumes

scenarios.name: lost_resumes_in_window
scenarios.note: inside the window a lost spurt that orders first comes back over a spurt granted after the loss (a sub-second hiccup)

scenarios.name: lost_dead_newer_keeps
scenarios.note: past the window a lost spurt is dead: its frames are dropped, and a spurt granted after the loss keeps the floor although the dead one orders first

scenarios.name: lost_yield_keeps_window
scenarios.note: a lost spurt whose frame comes back inside the window while a spurt that orders first holds the floor yields, but keeps the lost spurt's window: a backlog after it is dropped and the spurt ends

scenarios.name: bench_2026_11_04
scenarios.note: the bench failure: held 16 s, lost, another talker granted, the backlog arrives 13 s after the loss; the live talker keeps the floor and the backlog is not forwarded

scenarios.name: stall_is_not_silence
scenarios.note: a pass longer than the quiet timer is not counted as silence; frames queued during it count from when they were received

scenarios.name: lost_bound_local_stall
scenarios.note: floor lost is max(5 s, 1.5 x stall p99): 6 s gives 9 s

scenarios.name: lost_bound_capped
scenarios.note: and at most 15 s

scenarios.name: talk_limit
scenarios.note: a spurt is ended 1 s past its talk limit

scenarios.name: release_tombstones
scenarios.note: a release ends the spurt; a late claim and frames are refused; an overtaking release blocks its claim

scenarios.name: keyed_on_identity
scenarios.note: an outsider's claim with a victim's tag is its own record; frames go to the live one

scenarios.name: superseded
scenarios.note: a talker's new spurt ends its old one

scenarios.name: capacity_eviction
scenarios.note: a full table evicts ended, then known, then yielded and lost; never live or pending

scenarios.name: counters_evict_lru
scenarios.note: replay counters keep the most recently advanced talkers

scenarios.name: phone_grant_limit
scenarios.note: a phone's claim, its GRANT, and its talk limit

scenarios.name: phone_retry_give_up
scenarios.note: no answer: two retries 600 ms apart, then the phone gives up

scenarios.name: phone_busy_needs_the_claim
scenarios.note: a BUSY counts only if it names a claim the phone holds

scenarios.name: phone_yield
scenarios.note: a YIELD naming a held claim stops the talker; a forged one does not

scenarios.name: phone_self_yield
scenarios.note: a phone that learns a better live spurt stops by itself

scenarios.name: phone_listener
scenarios.note: a listener: claim, TALKING, frames, quiet, release

scenarios.name: phone_relay_view
scenarios.note: a TALKING from the phone's relay retires a zombie that orders first (its RELEASE was lost); a frame of it brings it back if the TALKING was stale

scenarios.name: phone_stale_backlog
scenarios.note: a phone drops a lost spurt's frames and TALKING once the window is over: a newer live spurt is never yielded to it

scenarios.name: phone_end
